summary: Real-time stock visibility across locations, with control at piece and series level.
outcome: Piece-level truth, live across every location.

hero.headline: Know every piece. Stay in control.
hero.body: Track every piece across locations, movements and counts.

problemSection.title: Where stock counts lose the truth.
problemSection.intro: Three operational failures that turn a physical count into a negotiation, and an available piece into a refused sale.

problems.title: The count is a negotiation
problems.description: Conflicting counts cannot be traced back to the pieces behind them.
problems.quote: Rack says 38. System says 41. Nobody can name the three.

problems.title: Stock is in the wrong place, and nobody can see it
problems.description: Stock may exist elsewhere, but the counter cannot see where.
problems.quote: Sold out at the counter while the warehouse is holding forty.

problems.title: Identity is lost at receiving
problems.description: Shared style codes erase the intake, cost and price trail.
problems.quote: A return arrives and nothing says which entry it came out of.

consequence.title: None of this arrives as a loss. It arrives as time spent arguing, and as sales that quietly did not happen.

items.label: Variance without a cause
items.body: A difference is written off because no entry can be named as the one that is short.

items.label: Available stock refused
items.body: The counter turns a customer away while the piece sits in a location it cannot see.

items.label: Returns nobody can place
items.body: A piece comes back and no record says which intake, cost or price series it belongs to.

outcomesSection.title: Three things change about
outcomesSection.intro: Piece-level identity. Location-aware stock. A history that stays intact.

outcomes.title: A count that names the piece
outcomes.description: Stock audit compares physical scans against the entries the system is holding, so a variance points at a specific entry and location instead of producing a bare quantity gap.

outcomes.title: Availability that knows where it is
outcomes.description: Every line carries the warehouse or store holding it. The counter, the transfer screen and the stock list are all reading the same location-aware number.

outcomes.title: Movement that leaves a trail
outcomes.description: Transfers, damage entries and adjustments post against the same piece identity that receiving issued, so the history of a piece survives every hand it passes through.

groups.title: Stock visibility
groups.context: One list that answers what is on hand, what it is worth and where it is sitting.

groups.title: Piece & series identity

workflow.title: How stock actually moves
workflow.intro: Five operational steps. Each one hands the next a record rather than a spreadsheet row.

steps.title: Stock is received
steps.body: Goods arrive against a purchase and are opened as a stock entry for the receiving location.

steps.title: Identity is issued

steps.body: The line joins the stock list under the warehouse or store that physically holds it, with rate, MRP and tax attributes attached.
steps.record: Line live in the stock list

steps.title: Stock moves
steps.body: A transfer takes pieces out of the source location and leaves them awaiting receipt at the destination — the same identity on both sides.

steps.title: Stock is counted
steps.body: An audit scans what is physically there and compares it with the entries on file, so a difference names the entry it belongs to.

verticalRelevance.apparel: Size and colour are separate pieces, not one style quantity, so a rack that is short is short in a specific size rather than in the abstract.
verticalRelevance.jewellery: High-SKU assortments with near-identical designs stay separable, because the piece carries the barcode rather than the design name.
verticalRelevance.franchise: Every line names the outlet holding it, so head office reads one stock list without asking nine people for theirs.

seo.title: Inventory module
seo.description: Piece and series level stock control across warehouses, stores and partner outlets — barcodes issued at receiving, transfers, audits and damage entries on one record.
seo.ogTitle: Bizonix Inventory — piece-level stock, live by location
seo.ogDescription: Stock held as pieces against the location that has them, with barcode identity issued at intake and carried through every movement.

faqs.question: Is stock tracked per piece or per batch?
faqs.answer: Both are represented. A stock entry holds the intake — what was opened, what has sold and what remains — and individual pieces within it carry their own barcode. That is why a variance can name an entry instead of reporting a bare quantity gap.

faqs.question: We already have barcodes from an older system. Do they survive?
faqs.answer: Existing codes are held against the new barcode as the legacy code, and both appear on the printing screen. Scanning history and old labels stay meaningful while the new identity takes over.

faqs.question: Does the stock number differ by location?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every line is held against the warehouse or store that has it, and the stock list can be read for one location or across them. There is no single blended figure that hides where stock actually is.

faqs.question: How are damage and shrinkage handled?
faqs.answer: Through damage entries and adjustments, posted against the affected stock entry rather than typed over the quantity. The stock number changes and the reason for the change stays attached to it.

faqs.question: How often do we have to do a full count?
faqs.answer: That remains an operating decision. Stock audit supports counting a location or a section against the entries on file, so partial counts are meaningful on their own instead of only being useful once everything is counted.

outcome: Receiving, pricing and payables on one trail.

hero.headline: What you order is what arrives.
hero.body: Keep the order, the receipt and the shortfall on one document.

screen.alt: Bizonix purchases screen filtered by received, draft and cancelled, showing supplier, quantity, amount and status per purchase.

problemSection.title: Where purchases lose their trail.
problemSection.intro: Three breaks between agreeing an order, receiving what actually turned up, and knowing what a supplier is owed.

problems.title: The order and the receipt drift apart
problems.description: The order and the physical receipt stop sharing one record.
problems.quote: Ordered 120, received 108, and the file still reads 120.

problems.title: Landed cost stops travelling with the goods
problems.description: Stock keeps its selling price but loses the cost of its intake.
problems.quote: Margin is a guess because cost is an average of everything.

problems.title: The supplier position lives outside the system
problems.description: Purchases, returns and payments must be assembled by hand.
problems.quote: A payment run starts with a phone call to the supplier.

consequence.title: The order itself is rarely the problem. Everything downstream of it is rebuilt by hand.

items.label: Short receipts absorbed
items.body: A shortfall reaches the shelf before anyone notices, and no document is left holding the difference.

items.label: Margin as an estimate
items.body: Selling price is exact and cost is an average, so profitability is stated with more confidence than it has.

items.label: Payment runs by phone
items.body: What is owed to a supplier is reassembled from three places every time somebody asks.

outcomesSection.title: Three changes keep
outcomesSection.intro: From purchase to receipt, with costs and supplier context intact.

outcomes.title: One document from order to receipt
outcomes.description: A purchase moves through draft, received and cancelled states on the same record, so the quantity and the amount always describe the same transaction rather than two versions of it.

outcomes.title: Cost survives the put-away
outcomes.description: Purchase rate and cost stay attached to the stock the receipt opened, which is why the stock list can show cost and value alongside sale rate and MRP.

outcomes.title: A supplier position that is already assembled
outcomes.description: Purchases, purchase returns and payments post against the same supplier, so what is owed is read rather than reconstructed.

workflow.title: From commitment to shelf
workflow.intro: Procurement is a hand-off problem. These are the five hand-offs, and what the system is holding after each one.

steps.title: The purchase is raised
steps.body: A purchase is created against a supplier with the lines, quantities and rates being committed to. It sits in draft until it is acted on.

steps.title: Goods are received
steps.body: What physically arrived is receipted against that purchase. The purchase moves to received and the supplier's invoice reference is captured with it.

steps.title: Stock is opened
steps.body: The receipt opens a stock entry at the receiving location, carrying purchase rate, MRP and tax attributes across with it.

steps.title: Identity is printed
steps.body: Barcodes are issued for the received pieces and labels are printed before the goods are put away.

steps.title: The supplier position updates
steps.body: The received value and any purchase return post against the supplier, so payables reflect the goods that were actually accepted.

verticalRelevance.apparel: Season intakes arrive as many small consignments; each one stays separable, so a slow-moving colour can be traced back to the buy that brought it in.
verticalRelevance.jewellery: Designs repeat across suppliers, so holding the intake reference on the line is what keeps two visually identical items from merging into one cost.
verticalRelevance.franchise: Central buying keeps the cost on the record that is later transferred out, so an outlet is not receiving stock with an unexplained value.

faqs.question: Can we receive less than we ordered?
faqs.answer: Yes. Receiving is recorded against the purchase, so the received quantity can differ from the ordered quantity and the difference stays visible on the purchase rather than being edited away.

faqs.question: Which cost does the stock carry?
faqs.answer: The cost captured on the intake that opened the line. That is why the stock list can show purchase rate and cost next to sale rate and MRP for the same row.

faqs.question: How are supplier returns handled?
faqs.answer: As purchase returns posted against the supplier and the stock they came from, so both the stock position and the amount owed move together.

faqs.question: What is series pricing used for here?
faqs.answer: It lets an intake carry its own rate rather than inheriting a single price for the style, so two consignments bought at different rates stay priced as they were bought.

faqs.question: How does opening stock come in?
faqs.answer: Through the same purchase and receiving path, recorded as a system opening entry. The stock arrives with a reference attached instead of appearing as an unexplained quantity.

outcome: Every bill posts itself to stock and to books.

hero.body: Billing, stock and the counter's shift all close together.

problemSection.title: Where counter days stop closing.
problemSection.intro: Three failures that put the day's work back on somebody's desk long after the customer has left.

problems.title: The sale is typed twice
problems.description: Counter sales are re-keyed into stock and accounts after the day.
problems.quote: Yesterday's sales get entered tomorrow, from a printout.

problems.title: Nobody can close a counter
problems.description: Without shift boundaries, a cash difference has nowhere to belong.
problems.quote: The drawer is short and the day is the only suspect.

problems.title: Returns break the record
problems.description: A returned piece no longer points to the bill that sold it.
problems.quote: Two records for one piece, and stock believes both.

consequence.title: The counter is fast. Everything that happens behind the counter is not.

items.label: The day arrives late
items.body: Stock and books describe yesterday, because yesterday is still being typed in.

items.label: Shortfalls with no boundary
items.body: Cash cannot be attributed to a counter, a shift or a person, so the difference is absorbed.

items.label: Stock counted twice
items.body: A returned piece re-enters as new quantity while the sale that released it still reads complete.

outcomesSection.title: Three things change about
outcomesSection.intro: Billing, stock and books stay connected through the trading day.

outcomes.title: The bill posts itself
outcomes.description: Billing moves the piece out of the stock line it was held on and lands the sale value in the books. There is no end-of-day re-entry step to get wrong.

outcomes.title: A counter you can actually close
outcomes.description: Every order carries the counter it was raised at and the state of its payment, so the day can be read one counter at a time instead of as a single blur.

outcomes.title: A return that finds its bill
outcomes.description: Because the piece carries its own identity, a return posts against the sale that issued it — the stock goes back to a real line rather than becoming a new one.

steps.body: A billing session is started for the counter, so everything billed from here belongs to a shift that can be closed later.

steps.body: The barcode issued at receiving is read at the counter. Price, tax treatment and the stock line it belongs to come with it.

steps.title: Payment is taken
steps.body: The order records what was paid against what was owed, and the payment state moves with it.

steps.title: Goods are handed over

steps.title: The session is closed
steps.body: The counter is handed over against its own totals, and the day's sales are already sitting in the books.

seo.description: Retail counter billing with barcode scanning, billing sessions, cash handover and returns — every bill moving stock and books in the same pass.

faqs.question: What is a billing session for?
faqs.answer: It gives the day a boundary. Bills belong to a session at a named counter, so cash can be handed over against what that counter actually took rather than against a whole-day estimate.

faqs.question: Do we have to capture customer details for every sale?
faqs.answer: No. Orders can be raised as walk-in, and a name is attached only when it is useful — both appear on the same order list.

faqs.question: When does stock actually reduce?
faqs.answer: At fulfilment, when the goods are handed over. The order carries its fulfilment state, so a billed-but-not-yet-collected order does not silently disappear from stock.

faqs.question: How is a return connected to the original sale?
faqs.answer: Through the piece. The barcode scanned on the way out is the same one scanned on the way back, which is what lets the return post against the order it came from.

faqs.question: Can more than one counter bill at the same time?
faqs.answer: Yes. Each order records the counter it was raised at, which is what makes per-counter totals and separate handovers possible.

title: Wholesale
summary: Bulk orders, fulfilment, dispatch and partner credit without side systems.
outcome: Bulk orders that dispatch without a spreadsheet.

hero.headline: One order, billed and dispatched.
hero.body: Hold what was ordered, fulfilled and still owed on one record.

problemSection.title: Where bulk orders lose their shape.
problemSection.intro: Three failures that appear the moment an order leaves the warehouse in more than one consignment.

problems.title: Part-shipped orders lose their shape
problems.description: Partial consignments leave the outstanding quantity in a side file.
problems.quote: A pending list that lives in a spreadsheet on one laptop.

problems.title: Picking works from a printout
problems.description: Printed picks go stale while warehouse stock keeps moving.
problems.quote: Two orders promised the same forty pieces.

problems.title: Credit is an opinion
problems.description: Buyer exposure is rebuilt from billing, returns and receipts.
problems.quote: Nobody can say what a buyer owes without opening three files.

consequence.title: Volume is not the hard part. Holding one order together across three separate events is.

items.label: Pending held in memory
items.body: What is still due to a buyer survives in a side file that one person maintains.

items.label: Promises that collide
items.body: Two orders are committed against the same pieces because picking read a printout.

items.label: Exposure assembled by hand
items.body: A buyer's balance is rebuilt from billing, returns and receipts before every conversation.

outcomesSection.title: Three things change about
outcomesSection.intro: Orders, stock commitments and buyer positions stay on one record.

outcomes.title: An order that knows what is still outstanding
outcomes.description: Billing and fulfilment are tracked separately on the same order, so a partly dispatched order reads as partly dispatched rather than as done or not started.

outcomes.title: One stock pool, not a wholesale copy of it
outcomes.description: Wholesale sells from the same stock lines the counter and the warehouse read, so a commitment made in bulk is visible everywhere else immediately.

outcomes.title: A buyer position that is already assembled
outcomes.description: Bills, returns and receipts post against the same partner, so the amount outstanding is read off the record instead of being reconstructed.

workflow.title: From order to dispatch
workflow.intro: Bulk selling is a sequence of partial states. These are the five, and what the record holds at each.

steps.title: The order is raised
steps.body: A wholesale order is created against a buyer, with the lines, quantities and rates being committed to.

steps.title: Stock is drawn against
steps.body: The order is picked from the same stock lines everything else reads, so the commitment is visible to the counter and the warehouse at once.

steps.title: Goods are packed
steps.body: Fulfilment records what has actually been packed against the order, which may be less than the whole order.

steps.title: The consignment leaves
steps.body: Dispatch marks the packed goods as gone and leaves the unfulfilled remainder still open on the order.

steps.title: The buyer position moves
steps.body: The billed value, any return and any receipt post against the buyer, so the outstanding amount reflects the goods that actually shipped.

verticalRelevance.jewellery: Assorted bulk lots are made of many small designs; fulfilment has to record which designs were actually packed, not just a carton count.
verticalRelevance.franchise: The same fulfilment path serves partner outlets, which is why a franchise transfer and a wholesale dispatch behave like relatives rather than strangers.

faqs.question: Can an order be dispatched in parts?
faqs.answer: Yes. Fulfilment is recorded against the order rather than replacing it, so a partly shipped order keeps its remainder open instead of being closed early or duplicated.

faqs.question: Does wholesale keep its own stock?
faqs.answer: No. It sells from the same stock lines as the counter and the warehouse. That is the point — a bulk commitment is visible to everyone reading stock, immediately.

faqs.question: Can wholesale buyers have their own rates?
faqs.answer: Rates are set on the order, and series pricing lets an intake carry its own rate, so partner pricing does not force a change to the master price of the style.

faqs.question: How is buyer credit tracked?
faqs.answer: Bills, sales returns and receipts post against the same partner record, so the outstanding position is read from the account rather than assembled before each conversation.

faqs.question: What happens when a partner sends stock back?
faqs.answer: A sales return posts against the order it came from and moves the stock back into the location that receives it, so both the goods and the amount owed move together.

title: Franchise

outcome: Autonomy at the outlet, oversight at the centre.

hero.headline: One network. Every outlet visible.
hero.body: Give partners independence while head office reads one position.

problemSection.title: Where networks lose visibility.
problemSection.intro: Three failures that reduce a network of outlets to a summary assembled at the end of the month.

problems.title: Outlets operate off-system
problems.description: Head office reconstructs outlet sales from month-end summaries.
problems.quote: The network's stock position is a WhatsApp thread.

problems.title: Transfers sit in limbo
problems.description: Dispatch and receipt live apart, leaving stock between owners.
problems.quote: Sent 48. Received 44. No document holds both numbers.

problems.title: Visibility and control get confused
problems.description: Visibility often grants too much control or too little information.
problems.quote: Either everyone is an admin, or nobody can see anything.

consequence.title: The brand is distributed. The record of the brand is not.

items.label: A network described monthly
items.body: What sold, at what price, and what is still on a shelf all arrive after the fact.

items.label: Stock that belongs to nobody
items.body: Between dispatch and receipt the goods sit outside every location's record.

items.label: Access as a blunt switch
items.body: Visibility can only be bought with control, so brands over-share rights or under-see the network.

outcomesSection.title: Three things change about
outcomesSection.intro: Independent outlets. Connected movements. A shared operating view.

outcomes.title: The outlet is a real boundary, not a filter
outcomes.description: Each franchise operates as its own entity with its own stock and counters, so partner autonomy is a structural fact rather than a permission that can be forgotten.

outcomes.title: A transfer that has two ends

faqs.question: Does head office control the outlet's day-to-day?
faqs.answer: No. The outlet operates as its own entity — its own stock, its own counters and its own users. The centre reads the network position; it does not have to bill on the partner's behalf to see it.

faqs.question: What happens between dispatch and receipt?
faqs.answer: The stock is out at the source and awaiting receipt at the destination. Both states sit on the same transfer, so goods in transit are never unaccounted for.

faqs.question: Do outlets have to maintain their own product data?
faqs.answer: Product masters are shared, so a style means the same thing everywhere in the network. Stock, orders and counters remain the outlet's own.

faqs.question: What if an outlet receives less than was sent?
faqs.answer: The difference stays visible on the transfer rather than being absorbed. The conversation then starts from a document instead of from two conflicting counts.

faqs.question: How is partner access restricted?
faqs.answer: Through entity scope in the Security module — a user is attached to the entity they work in, which is what keeps one outlet from reading another.

faqs.question: When does an operating document reach the books?
faqs.answer: As part of the same flow that creates it. A bill, receipt or return is an accounting event as well as an operating one, which is why closing does not begin with an export.

faqs.question: Can we keep separate books per company or outlet?
faqs.answer: Yes. Books are held per operating entity, and reporting can be read for one entity or across the group.

faqs.question: What does GST support cover?
faqs.answer: Tax treatment is captured on the transaction — the stock line itself carries tax inclusion, tax rate and HSN — and GST reports are produced from those postings. The exact filing workflow should be confirmed against your own compliance process during a demo.

faqs.question: Can we get from a ledger line back to the transaction?
faqs.answer: That is the design intent of posting from documents: the entry exists because a document does, so the operating record behind a number is still identifiable.

faqs.question: How are opening balances handled at go-live?
faqs.answer: Through opening entries in the same structure, so the first period starts from a recorded position rather than an assumed one. The scope of migration is agreed during implementation.

steps.title: Scope is applied

steps.title: Work is done, and recorded

faqs.question: Can roles be defined for how we actually work?
faqs.answer: Roles carry permissions per function, so access can follow a real job — a counter user, a warehouse user, an accounts user — rather than a single administrator-or-not switch.

faqs.question: What exactly does entity scope control?
faqs.answer: Where a permission applies. A user attached to one outlet exercises their rights inside that outlet, which is what keeps a shared platform from becoming shared visibility.

faqs.question: Can franchise partners have their own logins?
faqs.answer: Yes — partner users are scoped to their own entity, so they run their outlet in the same product without reading the rest of the network.

faqs.question: What is kept about who did what?
faqs.answer: Actions are recorded against the documents they affect, so a change stays attached to the person and the entity behind it. Retention and export specifics are worth confirming against your own policy during a demo.

faqs.question: What can you say about hosting and certifications?
faqs.answer: Nothing is claimed here that has not been verified. Hosting arrangement, backup policy and any certification status should be confirmed directly during the demo rather than read off a marketing page.
